assign.request: add the Panel: clock element to the /framework/ page, this is badass.
assign.now: scoping — reading the panel() seam and the landing's tracks
steps: Read the seam: panel(), paint(), templates.clock, the landing's tracks
Decide the band: track, height, what it does at 3440
Land: log, readme, front-door console clean

log.msg: The T menu lied. `panel(fn)` builds `new Panel({draw: fn})`, so `data.template` stays unset and the bar's menu reads Panel.defaults.template — "blank" — while a clock is drawn. There was no door for "give me a panel showing X", which is exactly what the ask said. `panel()` now takes a T name as well as a function: `panel("clock")`. Two lines, no new export, and the call site reads like the request.

The height is the knob, not the width. The clock is `font-size: min(17cqw, 38cqh)`, so in any band wider than tall the HEIGHT sizes it — a fixed --panel-height: 34em had the clock filling 74% of the band at 1280 and 32% at 3440, i.e. a 2986x612 box with 955px of clock in it. `clamp(20em, 26vw, 48em)` measures 54/51/46% at 1280/1920/3440 — one composition at every width, and the band grows with the screen instead of the gutters.

links.label: The front door, with the clock

assign.outcome: **The live clock is on the front door** — a full-bleed `ext/Panel` band between the code sample and the walls, ticking, with its real bar: hit `T` and the band becomes any of the other twenty-two templates. Two things came out of it. `panel()` now takes a T name (`panel("clock")`) as well as a draw function, because `panel(fn)` leaves `data.template` unset and the bar's menu was reading "blank" while a clock was drawn. And the band's height is `clamp(20em, 26vw, 48em)`, not a flat 34em: the clock is `min(17cqw, 38cqh)`, so height is what sizes it, and the flat value filled 74% of the band at 1280 but 32% at 3440. Measured 54/51/46% at 1280/1920/3440, light and dark, no console errors on /framework/, /framework/ext/Panel/ or /full/.
